title: First and Last: Alex Baker Takes the Trophy, His Brother Takes the Spoon
title_candidates: First and Last: Alex Baker Takes the Trophy, His Brother Takes the Spoon
Three Spoons and a Trophy: Alex Baker Wins TEG 18 the Hard Way
106, an 11 and a 10 — and 169 Points All the Same
The Ends of the Table Swap Places at Camiral
theme: Handicap golf as the great leveller: the man who wrote the worst round in the Tour course's history led TEG 18 from the fifth hole to the last, while at Camiral the ends of the table simply swapped occupants — a three-time Spoon holder lifting the Trophy, the defending champion collecting the Spoon, and the reigning Spoon holder putting on the Green Jacket.
tone: house — faithful, entertaining, tongue-in-cheek; Ronay/Peck register, always anchored to the card
opening_hook: Open on R4 H14 at the Stadium: Alex Baker making a 10 on a par 4 (b33) with the Trophy already effectively in his bag — the perfect image of a champion who spent four days doing spectacular damage and never once losing the lead — then loop back to the 46 points on Saturday that had already settled it.
foreshadow: Alex Baker arrives with 3 prior Wooden Spoons and the Spoon in 2 of the last 3 TEGs — the least likely leader in the field
Jon Baker arrives as defending Trophy champion (TEG 17) and holds the gross lead after R1 and R2
Gregg Williams arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder (TEG 17) and opens with a 9 and an 8 on the Tour course
David Mullin, nine-time Jacket winner, is bottom of the pile by the 15th hole of the tournament after an 11

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Alex Baker (169 pts, by 8 from John Patterson)
competitions.how: Decided on day one and defended thereafter: Baker's 46 in R1 was best in field and 12 clear, and he was never headed again after taking the outright lead at R1 H5. Patterson actually outscored him in R2 (-1) and R4 (-4), but never got the deficit under 8; win_anatomy calls it 'inherited' — Baker was the steadiest man in the field (never worse than 3rd of 5, consistency rank 1) while the chasers gave shots back faster than they took them. Even an ordinary round in place of Patterson's worst would not have flipped it.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (+66, by 14 from David Mullin)
competitions.how: Built, not inherited, and built from a ruin: Williams opened with a 9 at the 7th and an 8 at the 17th on the Tour course and sat 3rd, then went best-in-field in R2 (+14), took the outright gross lead at R3 H2 as Jon Baker's challenge disintegrated, and shut the door with a best-in-field +12 in R4 — a new personal best 84 at the Stadium. Beat Mullin head-to-head in 3 of the 4 rounds; the 8-shot cushion after R3 became 14 by the close.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.winner_or_loser: Jon Baker (126 pts, 23 adrift of David Mullin)
competitions.how: Comprehensive. Bottom of the field in R1, R3 and R4, below the field median in all four rounds, and never once posted a best-in-field round. He had actually led the Jacket after 36 holes; the collapse came at the Stadium — bottom of the Spoon table for good at R3 H2, a 9 at the 4th two holes later, and a 28-point round that put him 16 behind Mullin in a single day. Mullin outplayed him in 3 of the 4 rounds and the gap still finished at 23.

headline_candidates: Forty-Six and Farewell: Alex Baker Wins TEG 18 on Saturday
Patterson Bleeds 22 Shots in Eight Holes While Baker Counts His Points
Mullin Makes 11 at the 15th and Discovers the Bottom of the Table
rounds.chosen_headline: Forty-Six and Farewell: Alex Baker Effectively Wins TEG 18 on Saturday
rounds.angle: The tournament's decisive round dressed up as an opening one: Baker's 46 points on the Tour course opened a 12-point lead that nobody ever reduced, while Patterson haemorrhaged 22 shots between the 3rd and the 10th, Williams made a 9 and an 8, and Mullin's 11 at the 15th dropped him to the foot of the field.

headline_candidates: 106: The Champion Writes the Tour Course's Worst-Ever Card
An 11, an 8, and an Eleven-Point Lead Still Standing
Patterson Posts a Personal Best and Gains One Shot on the Leader
rounds.chosen_headline: 106: The Trophy Leader Writes the Worst Card in the Tour Course's History
rounds.angle: Alex Baker's 106 gross — an 11 at the 18th, an 8 at the 16th — is the worst round in 22 prior TEG visits to the Tour course, and he still went to bed 11 clear on Stableford; behind him Patterson made a personal-best 94, Williams turned 31 points into 42, and Jon Baker's tidy finish left him holding a gross lead he had four holes of R3 left to enjoy.

headline_candidates: Eighty-Four, and Still Eight Behind: Mullin Rewrites the Stadium Record
The Best Round in TEG History at Camiral Buys Precisely Nothing
Two Holes on Monday Cost Jon Baker Everything
rounds.chosen_headline: Eighty-Four, and Still Eight Behind: Mullin Rewrites the Stadium Record on Monday
rounds.angle: The round of the tournament and the round of the record book belong to Mullin — 84 gross, seven better than his own Camiral best and five better than the course record across 27 prior visits — and it gained him one shot on Williams, who took the outright gross lead at the 2nd and never gave it back; the same two holes dropped Jon Baker to the bottom of the Spoon table for good, a 9 at the 4th confirming it.

headline_candidates: A 10 at the 14th, and the Trophy Anyway
Williams Signs for 84 and the Jacket; the Bakers Finish First and Last
Thirteen Clean Holes for Williams, Six Shots Gone in One for Baker
rounds.chosen_headline: A 10 at the 14th, and the Trophy Anyway
rounds.angle: Baker's coronation round contains a sextuple bogey and a quadruple, and it doesn't matter a jot; Williams closes with 13 consecutive holes without dropping a net shot and a personal-best 84 for a 14-shot Jacket, Patterson birdies the 17th to salvage a last flourish, and the brothers Baker collect the Trophy and the Spoon from the same clubhouse.

players.arc: Three prior Wooden Spoons and the Spoon in two of the last three TEGs, and he leads from the fifth hole of the tournament to the last — 169 points, the seventh-best Trophy total on record, built on a 46 in R1 and defended through a 106, an 11, a 10 and two quadruple bogeys.

Reigning Wooden Spoon holder opens with a 9 and an 8 and finishes as the only man in the field improving every single round — 42 points and best-in-field gross in R2, outright Jacket lead at R3 H2, a personal-best 84 at the Stadium in R4 and the Green Jacket by 14.

Defending Trophy champion, gross leader after 36 holes, and then two holes at the Stadium on Monday: bottom of the table at R3 H2, a 9 at the 4th, and no round above the field median all tournament — the Spoon by 23.

Ran up an 8 in R1 and another in R2 and still finished runner-up, outscoring the champion in two of the four rounds, setting personal bests on both courses and birdieing the 17th on the final day — comfortably the best week of anyone who never led.

Nine Jackets to his name; makes an 11 at the 15th on the opening day, sits bottom of the field by nightfall, then shoots the lowest round in TEG's history at the Stadium — 84 — and still loses the Jacket by 14 and finishes fourth of five.

venue_notes: TEG's 4th visit to Catalonia and a familiar double bill at Camiral (PGA Catalunya), Girona: R1–R2 on the Tour course (the 5th and 6th TEG rounds there, Saturday and Sunday), R3–R4 on the Stadium (the 6th and 7th, Monday and Tuesday). Frame the Tour course as the 'more forgiving sibling' — and then note it yielded both the worst round in its TEG history (Alex Baker's 106) and Patterson's personal best; frame the Stadium, Spain's premier championship test, as the course that gave up its record to Mullin's 84 and then a matching 84 to Williams two days later. TEG 11 and TEG 12 are the reference points for almost every personal best here — worth noting how long these men have been coming back.
course_history_notes: Mullin's 6th visit to the Stadium: 84 gross in R3 — a personal best there by 7 (prior best 91, TEG 11), 8 better than his last visit, and a new TEG course record beating 89 across 27 prior visits (cr01).
Williams's 6th Stadium visit: 84 gross in R4 — a personal best by 8 (prior best 92, TEG 12) and 8 better than his last visit; the Jacket was won on his best-ever golf at the venue.
Patterson set new personal bests at both courses: 94 at the Tour in R2 and 93 at the Stadium in R3 — the runner-up's week was genuinely his best Camiral golf.

Alex Baker went the other way: 7 shots worse than his last Stadium visit and, with the 106 in R2, the worst round recorded on the Tour course in 22 prior TEG visits (cr02) — and won the Trophy regardless.
decisive_moments: Trophy — R1 on the Tour course: Alex Baker's 46 points, best in field by 12, taken outright at H5 and never surrendered across the remaining 67 holes (b46, b02).
Green Jacket — R3 H2 at the Stadium: Williams pars, Jon Baker's 20-hole gross lead ends, and the outright lead changes hands for the last time; 8 clear that evening, 14 by Tuesday (b34, b03).

Wooden Spoon — R3 H2 at the Stadium: Jon Baker drops to the bottom of the table for the final 52 holes, the 9 at the 4th two holes later confirming a 28-point round and a 16-point loss to Mullin in a single day (b44, b19).

vehicle_fit_response.note: The inventory of blow-ups is real (Alex Baker alone: 106, an 11, a 10, two quads) but it works as texture inside the winner's story rather than as the frame — and catalogue led two of the last three reports; the genuinely rare thing here is a three-time Spoon holder winning the Trophy while the defending champion took the Spoon.

why_the_champion_won: He banked the entire margin on day one — 46 points, best in field by 12 — and then simply refused to fall over: never worse than 3rd of 5, the steadiest man in the field round to round, while Patterson (who outscored him in two rounds) never assembled four days good enough to erase a lead that was handed over at R1 H5 and never returned.
